title: Squad Based Roguelite made with Opus in 2 weeks
author: AdamAlexandr
selftext:
I built this game called Space Marines 2. It's a tactical roguelite inspired by Aliens and Space Hulk. It's entirely made by LLM including all code, graphics and sounds. Mostly it's me talking to the claude app on my phone to control my desktop session running \`/remote-control\`.

It's built on Typescript/ThreeJS and took about 2 weeks. I wanted to share some aspects of its workflow.

**Graphics**

All graphics, including 3D modelling, textures and animations are done by Opus. The dedicated 3D AIs like Tripo can probably give better looking results. But there are some advantages using LLMs I really like.

I have a little JS library the ai calls functions from to define a 3D mesh in code. It writes code for each model that generates a GLTF. I think it helps the AI with the functional requirements of the model. It has full context of the games code, so it has context how the model is intended to be used.

**Debugging and Play Testing**

I had the AI write a bot that plays the game automatically. During the development, the bot would be playing the game onscreen continuously. It really helped to surface design issues quickly, without needing much focus.

**Overnight Loops**

Something that didn't go well was letting the AI go wild in overnight loops. Letting it flex it's own creative muscle and then seeing what it had done the next day.

I found this a bit addictive, but it always ended up disappointing. The AI isn't very good at game design and would come up with all these weird and overly complex mechanics that I'd discover much later. These weird rules influenced the AI in later sessions in ways I couldn't anticipate (because I didn't know they existed). And they took a long time tracking down and cleaning up...

**Code Locality**

To avoid bugs, I had the AI write the games code in terms of a library called [Spoke](https://github.com/Adam4lexander/Spoke). It's in C# but I ported it to javascript for this project. It's a bit like React except it can be used for anything. Including game mechanics. I find it really helps to reduce the number of bugs the AI writes, because it enforces strong code locality.

  
If you want to try, the link is here:

[https://adamalexandr.itch.io/space-marines-2](https://adamalexandr.itch.io/space-marines-2)
